requirements.quote: /home/user/backup/project_backup.tar.gz exists, is non-empty, and “tar -tzf” shows it begins with “project/”.
It has to be a valid gzip-compressed tar archive containing the complete /home/user/project tree, starting at its top-level directory (i.e. the first entry shown by “tar -tzf” must be “project/”).

check.cmd:
python3 -c 'import os, sys, tarfile
t = tarfile.open("/home/user/backup/project_backup.tar.gz", "r:gz")
names = {m.name.rstrip("/") for m in t.getmembers()}
need = [os.path.relpath(os.path.join(d, f), "/home/user") for d, _, fs in os.walk("/home/user/project") for f in fs]
sys.exit(0 if need and all(n in names for n in need) else 1)'

requirements.quote: /home/user/backup/project_backup.tar.gz.sha256 exists, contains one correctly-formatted line, and that the digest inside matches the actual SHA-256 of the archive.

check.cmd:
python3 -c 'import hashlib, re, sys
c = open("/home/user/backup/project_backup.tar.gz.sha256").read()
m = re.fullmatch(r"([0-9a-f]{64})  project_backup\.tar\.gz\n", c)
h = hashlib.sha256(open("/home/user/backup/project_backup.tar.gz", "rb").read()).hexdigest()
sys.exit(0 if m and m.group(1) == h else 1)'

requirements.quote: /home/user/backup/backup_status.log has a *new* final line that exactly follows the required semicolon-separated format and carries the same digest and byte-size found above.

check.cmd:
python3 -c 'import hashlib, os, sys
p = "/home/user/backup/project_backup.tar.gz"
h = hashlib.sha256(open(p, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
exp = "BACKUP_COMPLETED;FILE=project_backup.tar.gz;SIZE=%d;SHA256=%s" % (os.path.getsize(p), h)
l = open("/home/user/backup/backup_status.log").read().splitlines()
sys.exit(0 if l and l[-1] == exp else 1)'
